Extract the m-th Sample of Sigma or sd_num

get_Sigma.Rd

These two parameters are saved under different formats or transformation. These functions return the m-th sample of the corresponding parameter even if it has to be transformed from another equivalent saved parameter.

Usage

get_Sigma(draws, m, settings, g = NA, howsave = "data.frame", 
          Sigmacols, InvSigmacols, sdSigmacols, corSigmacols)  
get_sd_num(draws, m, settings, y = NA, howsave = "data.frame")

Arguments

draws

samples of model parameters in either list or data.frame (matrix) structure.

m

an iteration to choose.

settings

a matrix of model settings (in output of clustglmm).

g

a cluster label.

y

a name of an outcome.

howsave

the format under which draws is saved.

Sigmacols

columns in draws where Sigma matrix is stored, found automatically if missing.

InvSigmacols

columns in draws where InvSigma matrix is stored, found automatically if missing.

sdSigmacols

columns in draws where sdSigma is stored, found automatically if missing.

corSigmacols

columns in draws where corSigma matrix is stored, found automatically if missing.

Details

From draws, only the m-th element is used, which slightly differs depending on howsave. Functions are able to detect group-specificity and dimension from settings.

If Sigma is group-specific, then only matrix for group g is returned. If Sigma is not saved among draws, then it is reconstructed from InvSigma and inversion. If neither of Sigma and InvSigma is saved among draws, then it is reconstructed from standard deviations sdSigma or corSigma. If none of the above, a warning is triggered and diagonal unit matrix is returned.

The columns where the results are stored are found through function grep with pattern composed of the name of the parameter and the cluster label if given. This could be time-consuming, especially, when repeating over many m values. Hence, there is an opportunity to supply the columns via Sigmacols, InvSigmacols, sdSigmacols and corSigmacols.

On the other hand get_sd_num returns standard deviations for all clusters if cluster-specific. First, it tries to get it from sd_num, if saved. If not it transforms either from prec_num or var_num. If none of the above, error is triggered.

Value

A single covariance matrix Sigma or standard deviation(s) of numeric outcome y.

References

Vávra, J., Komárek, A., Grün, B., Malsiner-Walli, G. Clusterwise multivariate regression of mixed-type panel data. Stat Comput 34, 46 (2024). https://doi.org/10.1007/s11222-023-10304-5

Author

Jan Vávra

See also

clustGLMM

Examples


### Get some longitudinal mixed type data
### here generated by generate_longitudinal_mixed_type_data()
data("longitudinal_mixed_type_data")

# Examples here demonstrate the basic use of the available functions on a toy dataset.
# For more thorough analyses see the vignettes.


###-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
###     Prepare inputs for clustGLMM()
###-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
id <- "i"

family <- c("num", "poi", "bin", "ord", "cat")
names(family) <- Ys <- c("ynum", "ypoi", "ybin", "yord", "ycat")

## Create list of formulae for each outcome
formula <- list()
for(y in Ys){
  formula[[y]] <- list()
  formula[[y]]$fixed <- ~ f
  formula[[y]]$group <- ~ x
  formula[[y]]$random <- ~ 1
  formula[[y]]$offset <- ""
}
formula

# since it appears in $group which has a preference over $fixed

## All other inputs need to be prepared,
## unless the default values are desired (varying, save, howsave, param, tuning).
## See the vignette for how these can be adjusted.

###-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
###     Calling clustGLMM()
###-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

Gmax <- 5     # maximal number of mixture components to be considered
nchains <- 2  # number of chains to be sampled 

## No inits specified
set.seed(123456789)
mcmc <- clustGLMM(formula = formula, id = id, family = family, 
                  data = longitudinal_mixed_type_data, 
                  G = Gmax, iter = 100, nchains = nchains)

###-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
###     Getting Sigma matrix and sd_num
###-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# We take the last generated value by m = mcmc$iter

Sigma <- get_Sigma(mcmc$draws[[1]], mcmc$iter, mcmc$settings[[1]],
                   1, howsave = mcmc$howsave)
sd_num <- get_sd_num(mcmc$draws[[1]], mcmc$iter, mcmc$settings[[1]],
                     "ynum", howsave = mcmc$howsave)
